```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(reindeer)
src <- demo_corpus()@basePath
work <- tempfile("arch_"); dir.create(work); file.copy(src, work, recursive = TRUE)
corp <- corpus(file.path(work, basename(src)))
```

Archives and repositories want a README, a citation file and a machine-readable
record. reindeer writes all of them from the metadata you already keep.

## What is generated

```{r describe}
set_metadata(corp, list(
  Project = "Demo speech corpus",
  Description = "Read speech from a small demonstration database.",
  License = "CC-BY-4.0",
  team = list(list(name = "Fredrik Nylén", affiliation = "Umeå University"))))
files <- describe_corpus(corp, verbose = FALSE)
basename(files)
```

| File | For |
|------|-----|
| `README.md` | people |
| `CITATION.cff` | GitHub, Zenodo, reference managers |
| `datacite.json` | DOI registration |
| `_corpus_jsonld.json` | schema.org / search engines |
| `<name>_cmdi.xml` | CLARIN infrastructure |

## Kept up to date

After a metadata write, the files reindeer owns are regenerated if (and only
if) the metadata changed. Files reindeer did not create are never overwritten unless you pass `force = TRUE`. Opening a corpus never writes anything.

```{r auto}
set_metadata(corp, list(team = list(list(name = "Ada Lovelace"))))
grep("family-names", readLines(file.path(corp@basePath, "CITATION.cff")), value = TRUE)
```

Switch the automatic step off with `options(reindeer.auto_cmdi = FALSE)`.

## Export elsewhere, validate

```{r export}
out <- file.path(work, "export")
describe_corpus(corp, output_dir = out, formats = c("cff", "datacite"), verbose = FALSE) |>
  basename()
```

```{r validate, eval = FALSE}
validate_cmdi(file.path(corp@basePath, "ae_cmdi.xml"))   # against the CLARIN profile
```

CMDI profiles: `"speech-corpus"` (default), `"media-corpus"`,
`"speech-corpus-dlu"`; add `"session-cmdi"` to `formats` for one record per
session and bundle.
